cadence: weekly, Monday before the US open
method: Every Monday each open call is re-examined against the claims its note made. The numbers are computed from the record: where the call stands against what the note called for, how far the stop is, and a price-only range for where it can finish, drawn from the position's own recent volatility with no view assumed. The verdict is a judgment, stated with dated evidence: each claim the note relied on is re-measured and marked as holding or not, and the verdict has to follow from those marks. A broken thesis closes the call on the Scorecard from the review date. The return a note called for is written once and never changed.

latest.book_now: After this week's review the book holds four calls: the S&P 500 put against widening credit, long US energy stocks, long the yen and long US natural gas. Two reasons are fully in place and two are weakened. The put is the book's story: the index fell 4.9% from the entry close, more than the 3.2% the five earlier cases called for, and the put is worth about 38 a share against the 11.71 paid, a gain of about 225%, with three sessions to the planned close on Wednesday. We take half of that off now and let the rest run to the close. The energy call went the other way: oil fell 13% in a week on hopes of a negotiated end to the Iran war, the fund fell 12% and is 5.5% under entry, and the bond-yield half of its setup has handed back more than half of its rise, so we cut it to half size while oil is still expensive enough to keep the thesis alive. The yen call is flat with Tokyo still on the record as ready to act and the Bank of Japan leaning toward a December rise, and the gas call has delivered in the commodity, where gas is up 6% from entry and the oil-to-gas gap has closed from both ends as the note said, but the fund has given it all back to contract rolls and sits 8% under entry; we hold what is left of both. Credit and the put carry the most conviction this week, energy stocks the least. A reader holding the calls trims the put and the energy fund today and leaves the yen and gas positions as they are.

book.basis: equal weight across the open calls, one unit each, trailing 63 sessions; a 21-session driftless range

book_risk.note: correlations are of daily mark changes over the trailing 63 sessions; exposure is the position's % move per 1% in equities or the dollar and per +10bp in the 10-year yield

calls.title: Oil carries a war premium. US natural gas carries none.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate: median front-month gas gain over three months after an oil-to-gas ratio reading at or above the 95th percentile (42 episodes since 2004)
calls.expected_basis: the note's full-sample median target of 3.05 is 1.7% above Friday's 2.998, and the fund gives back about that much again on the December-to-January contract roll later this month, so from 8% under entry we expect a finish of about 9% under entry
calls.view_now: The gap the note was built on has closed the way it said it would: oil fell 13% in the week on hopes of an end to the Iran war while gas rose to 3.00, up 6% from entry and within 2% of the target, and the ratio has come in from the 96th to the 92nd percentile. The fund has received none of it, sitting 8% under entry, because the two contract rolls since September cost more than the gas price gained. Funds still hold the largest short in three years and are adding to it, which is fuel for a sharp rise if the mild November forecast turns cold, and the exit is 18% away, so we do not call the thesis broken; but with the extreme mostly closed and another roll ahead we expect the call to finish about where it is, with roughly a one-in-four chance of getting back to even.
calls.action_reason: Hold what is left after last week's trim and do not add. The gas price has nearly reached the target the note set and every condition still holds, so the thesis is not broken; the record short in gas and an exit 18% away justify carrying the remainder to the planned close on Dec 11, where a cold turn is the only route back to even
calls.weakened_reason: The thesis has largely played out in the commodity and the fund has not received it. Front-month gas is up 6% from entry at 2.998, within 2% of the 3.05 target, and the oil-to-gas gap has closed from the 96th to the 92nd percentile from both ends, but the fund the reader holds is 8% under entry because the November and December contract rolls cost it more than the gas price gained. With the gap now under the 95th-percentile line the edge was measured from, the remaining expected gas move is small and another contract roll lies ahead before the planned close

calls.title: Yields and oil are surging together. Energy stocks gained after that in 7 of 8 cases.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's expected return: the average fund return over six months in the eight earlier cases, with the 10% weekly-close exit applied
calls.expected_basis: the note's two cases with oil above $90 averaged +6.7%, but both had the bond-yield leg still rising, which this call no longer has, so we credit none of the eight-case average; from 5.5% under entry we weigh a recovery toward entry if the Iran talks fail against a close near the exit 10% under entry if a deal takes oil under about $83, and the two roughly balance to a finish about 2% under entry
calls.view_now: The reason for the call is weaker than at any point since it was made. Oil is still expensive, at the 87th percentile of three years, but it fell 13% in a week on reports of a draft proposal to end the Iran war even though no deal exists and attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz continued; the bond-yield half of the setup has given back more than half of its rise. The fund fell 12% in the week to 61.62, 5.5% under entry and 4.9% above its exit, and the broad market fell with it. We no longer expect the call to finish ahead: with the yield leg gone we stop crediting the eight-case average, and if a deal takes oil under about $83 the thesis breaks and the call most likely ends near the exit 10% under entry; if talks fail and oil holds above $90, the fund can recover toward entry.
calls.action_reason: Cut the position to half size. The move the call was built on in bond yields has handed back more than half of itself, the critical oil condition is one headline from breaking, and the fund is within 5% of its exit with a 64% base-rate chance of a move that size over the sessions left; we keep half because oil is still at the 87th percentile and the war has not ended, so the exit rule, not our view, decides the rest
calls.weakened_reason: Every line still holds, but half of the setup is gone and the other half is moving the wrong way. The note's cause was bond yields and oil surging together: the 10-year yield has handed back 56% of the rise the note was built on, and the daily check has flagged that since Oct 30. Oil, the critical half, fell 13% in the week on hopes of a negotiated end to the war and is now 9% above the line that would break the call. The fund fell 12% in the week to 61.62, 5.5% under entry and within 5% of its exit; over the sessions left, a move of that size down has happened about 64% of the time in the fund's own history

calls.title: The record yen rescue looks dead. So did the last three at exactly this point.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's target: 147 on dollar-yen by late January 2027, the median months-two-to-six move applied from 157.34, roughly +6% on the fund
calls.expected_basis: the median move of the three earlier campaigns, 6.9% on dollar-yen or about 6% on the fund, less the 0.7% already given up and a haircut for 38% of the window having passed with the move not begun; a quarter of the pattern's four-month window is now unavailable to it
calls.view_now: The driver is in place and nothing has moved against it: Tokyo repeated on Nov 2 that it is ready to act against disorderly moves, the minutes of the Bank of Japan's September meeting lean toward a December rate rise, and dollar-yen has spent eight weeks in a 156.5 to 158.6 range, closing Friday at 157.50, about where the call started. Price has done nothing in either direction: the fund is 0.7% under entry with 38% of the horizon gone and the move the pattern calls for not yet begun. We still expect the call to pan out, because in all three earlier campaigns the real move came in months two to six and this one is in month four of the campaign, but we shade the expected finish a little for the time that has passed with no start.
calls.action_reason: Leave the position as it is. The campaign stands, the Bank of Japan is leaning toward a December rise, speculators have not run ahead of the move, and the exit is 4% away; there is no new fact against the call, only the passage of time, which the pattern allows for

The Bank of Japan held its rate at 1.25% on Oct 30, and the minutes of its September meeting published this week showed members arguing for further rises, which the market reads as a December increase; strong US jobs data on Friday lifted the dollar

calls.title: Credit spreads widening, S&P 500 likely to close the gap
calls.called_for_basis: the note's expected return on the put, restated on Oct 29 when the Scorecard was corrected to mark the SPY 773 put the note told the reader to buy instead of the index: the put's modelled value if the S&P 500 falls the median 3.2% of the five cases by the planned close on Nov 11, about 24.5 a share against the 11.71 premium (+109%). Frozen at +3.2% on the index on Oct 26, before the correction
calls.expected_basis: the put's value at Friday's close, about 38 a share against the 11.71 paid: with the index already 4.9% under entry, past the 3.2% median fall of the five cases, and only three sessions left, the no-view range centres on where it stands now
calls.view_now: Both conditions hold and the call has done what it said: credit is at its widest since the move began at 348 basis points, and the S&P 500 fell 4.4% on Thursday to 7,377, which puts it 4.9% under the entry close after thirteen of the sixteen sessions, past the 3.2% median fall of the five earlier cases. The put the note told the reader to buy is worth about 38 a share against the 11.71 paid, a gain of about 225%, with three sessions to the planned close on Wednesday and the exit level 6% away. From here the put is 5% in the money, so the most likely finish is about where it stands; a 2% bounce in the index before Wednesday would still leave it roughly doubled, while a further fall adds about 7 a share for each 1% the index loses.
calls.action_reason: Take half the position off now and let the rest run to the planned close on Wednesday. The thesis has delivered more than the note called for, the gain is about 225% on the premium, and the three sessions left hold Tuesday's inflation report and a bounce risk after the worst day in nineteen months; halving locks in roughly the whole of what the note called for while keeping the rest on for the exit the scorer records
